newsitem.title: USA: Rottlund still committed to Orlando, Indianapolis.
newsitem.headline: Rottlund still committed to Orlando, Indianapolis.

text.p: Home builder Rottlund Co Inc said Monday it remains committed to operations in Orlando, Fla. and Indianapolis, Ind., despite a writedown of the value of the land.
"The writedown of land was required by a new accounting standard," said David Rotter, chief executive officer and president, in a statement.
"This writedown does not change our commitment to operations in the Orlando and Indianapolis markets," he said.

"We are continuing our efforts to complete our existing developments in Orlando and Indianapolis and continue to seek new land in these areas where we believe we can achieve higher absorption and margins," he said.

Earlier today, the company reported a loss for its fiscal fourth quarter ended March 31, 1997 of $668,000 or $0.11 a share compared with net income of $1.2 million or $0.21 during the same period last year. Included in the 1997 period is a noncash pretax writedown of $1.5 million representing an inventory valuation adjustment of certain land for about 250 unsold housing units located in Orlando and Indianapolis.
Fiscal fourth quarter revenues rose one percent from the same period a year ago to $38.1 million from $37.8 million.

For its fiscal year, Rottlund reported earnings fell 71 percent from a year ago to $1.2 million or $0.22 from $4.2 million or $0.74 a year earlier. Revenues for its fiscal year increased 37 percent to $180.4 million from $131.6 million.
Backlog at March 31, 1997 included 409 homes with a sales value of $60.9 million, 12 percent lower than the sales value of $69.3 million representing backlog of 533 homes at March 31, 1996.

New orders for 299 homes with a sales value of $43.4 million were received for the quarter ended March 31, 1997 compared with 414 homes with a sales value of $58.0 million for the same period in 1996, Rottlund said in a statement.
Trading in shares of Rottlund have resumed after a halt due to news pending. The shares were trading up 1/8 to 4-1/2.
